---
title: "P5 — Stress and biotechnology self-check"
---

Answer before opening the explanations. Explain one mechanism aloud and revisit
the [tutorial](index.qmd) if you can recall a term but cannot connect its steps.

## 1. Does survival establish unchanged fitness or yield?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Explanation

No. A surviving plant can have reduced growth, reproduction or seed viability. State and measure the actual performance outcome.
:::

## 2. Does short-term acclimation prove evolutionary adaptation?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Explanation

No. Acclimation occurs within an organism; adaptation involves heritable population change across generations.
:::

## 3. Are natural products necessarily harmless?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Explanation

No. Effects depend on compound, dose, exposure and the receiving organism.
:::

## 4. Does expression in guard cells prove a gene controls closure?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Explanation

No. Expression supports a location hypothesis. Causal evidence needs appropriate perturbations, controls and phenotype measurements.
:::

## 5. Why test multiple independent transformation events?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Explanation

To distinguish a reproducible consequence of the intended change from event-specific insertion, culture or background effects.
:::

## 6. Does more fluorescence prove detection of the intended chemical?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Explanation

No. Check specificity, background, calibration, timing and plant condition; other stimuli or measurement artefacts may change the signal.
:::

## 7. Name an empirical question and a value judgement in a biotechnology decision.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Explanation

Whether compatible relatives receive pollen is empirical. Who should decide an acceptable level of uncertainty involves values and governance. Both deserve explicit treatment.
:::
